problem: End-to-end image-to-action navigation policies are limited by scarce action-labeled data (imitation learning, with a straight-walking bias) and by the sim-to-real visual gap (RL in simulation). Prior temporal-distance predictors (ViNT, VIP) were treated as auxiliary signals and never evaluated in isolation.
motivation: Distance-to-goal can be mined from unlabeled video at internet scale without action labels, while low-level control transfers robustly when trained on geometric signals in simulation. Decoupling 'where to go' (perception) from 'how to go' (control) should give scalable semantics plus robust sim-to-real transfer.
key_idea: Train a self-supervised vision-language temporal-distance predictor (VLD) on ~3000 h of video, and train an RL policy in simulation on privileged geometric distance with learned overlap-conditioned noise, then swap in VLD predictions at deployment.
insight: Noise structure matters more than noise magnitude: policies trained with learned geometric-overlap noise (GeoNoise) transfer to VLD (SR 0.731), whereas OU noise of similar marginal variance collapses (SR 0.1145) because it lacks orientation-dependent errors that induce 360° scanning. Ordinal consistency (Kendall tau) tracks downstream navigation ranking (VLD > ViNT-Tuned > VIP-Nav). Ablations show the simulator's goal-directed trajectories are essential (real-world-only VLD collapses to tau≈0.1), the Gaussian-mixture NLL beats MSE/VIP/QRL, and negative mining is needed to recognize unrelated goals.
method: VLD architecture: frozen DINOv2-small image tokens and frozen CLIP text tokens (projected to DINOv2 space) form goal memory; a 4-layer Transformer decoder queries it from observation tokens, and CLS-token MLP heads output distance t̂≥0 and confidence ĉ∈[0,1]; missing modalities are masked so it supports image, text or joint goals.

Training objective: pairwise (o_i,o_j,j-i) sampling with td_max=100, ViNG-style negative mining (cross-trajectory pairs labelled td_max, p_neg=0.05), and an inlier-outlier Gaussian mixture NLL (σ_R²=4, σ_O²=40) that yields calibrated confidence.

Data: ~2949 h, comprising HM3D Habitat shortest-path trajectories (475k, with BLIP-bootstrapped text goals), 1720 h YouTube walking, Ego4D, and robot datasets (SCAND, GrandTour, CityWalker); frame rates are normalized to ~0.25 m per step.

Evaluation by ordinal consistency: Kendall's tau between predicted and ground-truth distances along trajectories at horizons of 20/50/100 steps, plus a pairwise distance-accuracy test for no-overlap viewpoints.

GeoNoise: an MLP takes 13-D overlap features (projection success ratio, relative rotation, SymLog translation) and predicts binned distributions over VLD's distance and confidence errors (trained by cross-entropy on VLD outputs); noisy values are sampled from it during RL to corrupt the privileged GT distance.

RL policy: PPO with an LSTM core; inputs are noisy distance and confidence, a frozen EfficientNet-B0 obstacle feature, GPS displacement and proprioception; the reward extends ZER with a PSR-based orientation penalty and a success bonus; at deployment VLD replaces the noisy GT distance zero-shot.

setting.backbone: VLD (frozen DINOv2-S + CLIP text, 11M trainable decoder) + PPO LSTM policy trained in simulation
setting.training_data: ~2949 h video: HM3D Habitat synthetic (1150 h, 475k trajectories), YouTube walking (1720 h), Ego4D 50 h, SCAND/GrandTour/CityWalker robot data (~29 h); BLIP-bootstrapped text goals; RL policy trained on Gibson in Habitat

setting.simulator: Habitat (Gibson for policy; HM3D for distance-function data)
setting.privileged: GT geometric distance-to-goal (plus overlap features) during RL training only; none at deployment (GPS/compass from odometry)

numbers_note: Distance-function results are Kendall tau on held-out validation trajectories (HM3D 0.82/0.70/0.61 at horizons 20/50/100; Gibson 0.84/0.73/0.71), not a standard benchmark. Real-world SR is reported inconsistently (93.3% vs 0.87 in the appendix text).
results: VLD (all data) reaches Kendall tau 0.82/0.70/0.61 on HM3D and 0.69/0.61 on in-the-wild data at horizons 50/100, clearly above ViNT-Tuned (0.67/0.56/0.48) and VIP-Nav. Swapped into the GeoNoise policy on Gibson it gets SR 0.731 / SPL 0.400, versus ViNT-Tuned 0.605 / 0.256 and VIP-Nav 0.279 / 0.115. It is below FGPrompt-EF in simulation (0.923 / 0.685) but beats it on a real robot (93.3% vs 60.0% SR).
limitations: The policy has no memory or map, so most failures are time-outs (62%) and near-match confusions (29%); the scalar distance interface discards information.

The real-world evaluation is small (15 trials, one environment), and the reported success rate is inconsistent (0.93 vs 0.87); the language-goal navigation policy is not evaluated in simulation or on the robot, only distance ordinal consistency.

Sim-only ImageNav performance lags the image-based FGPrompt-EF; the real-world-only VLD fails, showing dependence on synthetic goal-directed data; the GeoNoise model is calibrated to VLD's error patterns.
